Definition: cessation, i.e. an end (especially of the earth); often used adverb, no further; also the ankle (in the dual), as being the extremity of the leg or foot
BiblicalUsage: Ephes means an end, a ceasing — no further, the uttermost part. Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth; the Lord will judge His people when He sees their power is gone; is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may show the kindness of God unto him?
TheologicalSignificance: The ends of the earth are not too far for God's salvation, and the end of our strength is not the end of His mercy. I hold that both are where He begins, and that is why the call goes out to every end of the earth without exception.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
